About Event

The Fincantieri Maritime Dual-Use Hackathon comes to San Francisco, October 16–18.

Following the first edition in Rome, which brought together 70+ participants, including Italian Navy engineers, and produced five working prototypes, the challenge now crosses the Atlantic to the Bay Area’s deep-tech ecosystem.
Over 48 hours, engineers, developers, founders, researchers and designers will form teams to build working solutions around real maritime and defense engineering challenges , with access to technical mentors, development hardware and potential opportunities to continue developing the strongest concepts beyond the event.
Challenge Tracks
OT Cybersecurity & Blast Radius Analysis
Piping Layout Optimization
Software-Defined Vessel

Build with Real Hardware
Participants will have access to a selection of Qualcomm and Arduino technologies during the hackathon, including Snapdragon-powered laptops, edge AI and robotics development platforms, Arduino prototyping hardware and supporting developer tools.
These tools are intended for hands-on technical development . Participants with experience in areas such as software development, embedded systems, electronics, robotics, edge AI, computer vision or hardware prototyping will be best positioned to take full advantage of them.
Qualcomm and Arduino technologies will be introduced during the opening session so teams can quickly understand the available resources and integrate hardware, edge AI, computer vision, sensors or robotics into their prototypes.
Exact hardware configurations will be shared with participants ahead of the event.
More Than a 48-Hour Hackathon
The goal is not only to build a prototype, but to identify ideas with the potential to continue developing after the event.
Work on real Fincantieri challenges with potential relevance to future maritime and defense applications.

Compete for a Qualcomm-powered laptop awarded to the winning team.

Develop your concept beyond the hackathon: selected promising prototypes may have the opportunity to continue evolving.

Access Fincantieri expertise: winning and particularly promising concepts may receive mentoring from Fincantieri’s network of experts to help further mature the solution and explore its potential application within Fincantieri.

Connect with leading technical talent from industry, academia, venture capital and the defense innovation ecosystem.

Partners & Ecosystem
The hackathon is organized in collaboration with Naval Postgraduate School (NPS) and FLEETWERX.
Qualcomm is the main technology sponsor, supporting participants with hardware, development resources and technology expertise throughout the event.
Additional experts from Fincantieri, academia, industry, venture capital and the defense innovation ecosystem will support teams through mentoring and judging.
What to Expect
48 hours of hands-on building and prototyping

Real technical challenges provided by Fincantieri

Access to Qualcomm and Arduino hardware and development resources

Mentors and domain experts supporting teams throughout the event

Collaboration with engineers, founders, and researchers

A Qualcomm-powered laptop prize for the winning team

Potential follow-on development opportunities for the most promising concepts

No maritime background is required. However, this is a hands-on technical hackathon , and participants should be ready to contribute directly through software development, AI/ML, embedded systems, cybersecurity, robotics, engineering, CAD/optimization, product design or prototyping.
Come with a team or find one at the event.
To help us maintain an accurate headcount, a $20 refundable deposit is required to reserve your spot. The deposit will be fully refunded when you attend the event.
Spots are limited — register early to secure your place.

About Event

TrueFoundry Agent Harness Hackathon
AI agents are easy to prototype and much harder to run in production. Once an agent touches real users, tools, data, budgets, and internal systems, the work becomes less about a clever prompt and more about routing, permissions, tracing, retries, evals, guardrails, cost controls, and deployment.
Join TrueFoundry and HackerSquad for a full-day Agent Harness hackathon focused on building production-minded agentic applications. The goal is simple: take an agent use case from idea or prototype toward something that can be observed, governed, evaluated, and operated.
TrueFoundry's AI Gateway, Agent Gateway, and MCP Gateway will frame the day. Builders will work on practical agent harness patterns such as model routing, controlled tool access, MCP workflows, observability, eval loops, fallback behavior, budget controls, governance, and deployment paths.
This is a technical builder event, not a passive product pitch. Bring a laptop, a strong use case, and a willingness to build under realistic production constraints.
What You Can Build
An agent workflow with model routing, retries, and fallback behavior

A tool-using agent with controlled MCP or API access

An observability layer for traces, tool calls, latency, usage, cost, and failures

An eval or test harness for agent behavior across repeated runs

A governance pattern for permissions, approvals, logging, blocking, or escalation

A deployment-minded agent application that shows how it would run inside a real team or platform environment

Why This Gets Hard in Production
Agent systems need to coordinate models, tools, permissions, memory, context, retries, and fallbacks without becoming brittle one-off glue code.

Teams need traces, audit logs, usage visibility, cost attribution, and eval loops so they can understand what an agent did, why it did it, and what changed between runs.

Scaling agents means managing quotas, budgets, latency, provider failures, tool access, and security policies across teams.

Guardrails need to become runtime controls: clear rules for what data an agent can see, which tools it can call, which actions require human approval, and how unsafe requests or outputs get blocked, logged, or escalated.

Deployment gets harder when agents need to connect to internal systems, respect governance rules, and stay reliable as usage grows.

Platform, infrastructure, and backend engineers building or operating AI agent systems

AI engineers and product engineers working with LLMs, tool calling, MCP, evals, or agent workflows

Technical founders moving agent prototypes toward production

Security, DevOps, and ML platform practitioners thinking about governance, observability, and cost control

About Event

Build It. Test It. Prove It.
Smells like a hackathon. Runs like a pressure test, on you, not just your idea.
Proving Ground runs a three-day Sprint where judges push past the pitch. No script survives real questions about what you tried, what broke, and what you changed. That's harder to fake than a deck.
Past teams have gone on to raise from 500 Global and Blitzscaling Ventures, and been accepted into Berkeley SkyDeck and Confluent's accelerator, independently, without Proving Ground's involvement in those decisions.
What this is
Smells like a hackathon. Runs like a road test. A hackathon judges what you built by the end. A road test watches how you handle the car.
The team is almost everything. How you make decisions under pressure, how you handle a setback, how you treat each other when something breaks. You'll document that as you go. What we ask you to show and how we question it are built around behavior, not performance.
How it works
Over three days, founders build under real constraint. No script, no rehearsed demo. Judges probe what you tried, what broke, and what you changed, and compare where you started to where you ended.
Two Tracks
Discovery Track. Pre-market, no active customer contact yet. For the startup curious, including enterprise folks seriously exploring a leap.
Pre-seed Track. In-market, already talking to customers. Ship something real, show what's changed, pressure-test your next move.
After the Sprint
Select teams get invited into the Street Test: 30 days back in the real world, no artificial deadline, no audience. This is where we see if momentum was real or borrowed from the room. It's the part a hackathon can't offer, because a hackathon ends when the weekend does.

About Event

Sundai:
- a room full of people building moonshots - every sunday.

------

the loop is already spinning. More than 80% of Anthropic's code is written by Claude. Jeff Dean left Google after 30 years to build the loop for science. Direction-setting is the role left for humans.
the hard part: Lilian Weng's survey of harness engineering argues the near-term path to RSI runs through the harness rather than weight-rewriting. A self-improving meta-harness is within reach. The bottleneck is evals, because a loop is only as good as its evaluator. That's the hack.
in the room: researchers from MIT CSAIL, Harvard, DeepMind and Meta Reality Labs. Co-hosted by Autolab and Maritime (MIT spinouts), EdotEnv (YC S26), YN.app and Sundai .

------

We will build agents that recursively self improve, or train models using autoresearch principles. Every sunday we will focus on a different aspect of RSI.
✨Schedule✨
10:00 Intros
10:15 Idea pitching and team formation
14:00 Check in #1 and lunch
20:00 Check in #2 and presentations
✨What is Autolab✨
A platform for Autoresearch. Autolab.ai runs your ML experiments for you - agents plan, launch, and score thousands of training runs in parallel, on your GPUs, against your evals.
✨What is Sundai✨
Sundai is the largest AI hacker community at Harvard & MIT, now building weekly moonshots in SF. Every sunday we ask each attendee to work on a aspirational larger than life moonshot idea that they always wanted to work on. One sunday at a time. This is your chance to push yourself to next level. We had done 130+ hacks back-to-back in the last 2 years - one for every sunday without stopping
✨What is Maritime✨
Maritime.sh makes it easy to host personal AI agents, agentic apps, and specialized agents for groups of users. You can build an app where every user gets their own dedicated agent, managed and hosted through Maritime, with simple tooling like the Maritime CLI and SDK.
✨What is E.env✨
E.env builds self-improving RL envs to teach LLMs general research skills from Quant Research tasks. Market data is a great source of hard data science tasks and is self improving: as models trade better, the market becomes more efficient, which makes trading well harder again. E.env provides RL envs for post-training and eval services for agents.
✨Our mission at Sundai ✨
"Push the envelope of what is possible to do with AI in a day."
1. Grow the Best Hackers learn to build fast with AI
2. Build things that matter - measure in users $$$ / github ⭐️s
3. Spread the Hacker Mindset teach the skills that we learn
✨Our Principles✨
Build. Ship. Shortcuts
- Build: The purpose of Sundai is to get together and build moonshots. Every Sunday.
- Ship: get off the localhost . Deploy your learnings as a webapp or a post and a demo that works on the internet. Go for less, to do more.
- Shortcuts: Shortcuts is an ingenious move that a hacker makes to build a system that works. In order to build fast - you always need to think in shortcuts.

A twice-monthly working night for people building embodied AI. No robot required.
You built the arm at your kitchen table. You trained the policy overnight on your gaming rig. You collected the teleop data in your garage. The one thing none of it came with: labmates.
Degrees of Freedom is a monthly working night at Mission Robotics for everyone building physical AI without a lab around them. Bring the robot. Bring the sim that refuses to transfer. The person next to you has probably already hit your bug. Robotics failure is multidisciplinary: the fix is rarely in the field you know best. A room of mixed builders is the fastest debugger in the city.

About Event

For three years, using AI meant typing into a box and waiting for text to come back.
That era is ending.

The next interface isn't a chat window. It's worn, spoken, and always on.
Glasses that listen.
A pendant that remembers.
A tracker you never charge.
A second self that watches your screen and acts before you ask.
We're putting the founders building that future in one room with the people who want to build on it.

Half a day in San Francisco.

Real hardware on the table. Working demos, not slideware.
The lineup is a short list of founders shipping the wearables that are pulling AI off the screen.

The founders in the room:
Adam Cohen Hillel, Secondly - a personal AI "second self" that sees your screen and acts across every app you use. The chat box becomes a presence.

Nik Shevchenko, Omi - the open-source AI wearable necklace, with 250+ developer apps already built on it. Always listening, always yours.

AnhPhu Nguyen, Mira - AI smart glasses with no camera. They hear what you hear, recall every name, and translate 60+ languages in under a second. AnhPhu is the Harvard builder behind last year's viral I-XRAY demo.

Andy Kong, Chargerless - a 7-gram health tracker powered by daylight. One minute of sun a day and it never needs a charger.

What you'll build: pick a device, an API, or a live sensor stream.

Ship something a person could actually wear or talk to by the time we demo.

The strongest builds demo to the founders in the room.
This is for builders, hardware hackers, AI engineers, and designers who think the keyboard is a temporary technology.

About Event

A panel & mixer featuring Singaporean students who have pursued unique paths overseas and gained success based on their learnings from being abroad!
Hear from students part of overseas internship programmes such NUS Overseas College (NOC), NTU Overseas Entrepreneurship Programme (OEP) & SMU! They will share their perspectives on the startup ecosystem overseas, experiences navigating life and finding unique career opportunities away from home!
Our panelists include current students who have worked in startups in San Francisco, started their own startups funded by Y' Combinator and built large student communities! Learn from their journey working across multiple international cities, building powerful international networks , and taking unconventional paths of success .
Get ready for tips on:
Insights on working/studying abroad and how global perspectives benefit students

Building a strong professional network that sets you up for career success in Singapore & overseas

Maximizing your study/work abroad experience (including tricks to save money/maximize government grants)

Breaking into the startup world with your own startups or securing lucrative jobs & internships in San Francisco (Silicon Valley) & more!

All students, friends and working professionals are welcome (not limited to the included universities)! After the panel, there will be an active mixer with a guided element to ensure maximum connections! Food & Drinks will be provided🍕🥤
Speakers:
Jamie Yau - Co-Founder @ Collar (YC F26), SMU
Jamie Yau co-founded of Collar (YC F26), the platform for AI-native private market investors. Prior to founding Collar she worked as the Chief of Staff of Openspace Capital ($800M AUM), a venture firm based in Singapore.
Raymond Loong Ng - Co-Founder @ Neural Drive, NUS CS
Raymond Loong is a serial founder who has built and raised $300K+ across multiple AI ventures including Resumify, Singapore Youth AI, & Neural Drive AI. He has won 26/40 hackathons across Singapore, Vietnam, Shenzhen, and San Francisco and has been featured in The Straits Times, Business Times, and Lianhe Zaobao.
Jack Chen Lexin - AI Engineer @ Pokee AI, Founder @ OpenMentor, NUS CS & NOC SV 26'
Jack Chen is an AI Engineer @ Pokee AI & the founder of OpenMentor, Singapore's largest student mentorship community, engaged over 50k students, clients include Notion, Manus, Hoyouverse, Tavily and 30+ more.
Moderator:
Raymond Lim - NTU Y4 Computer Engineering, NTU OEP Shanghai 24', SV 25', NTU-USA SV 26', GEM Ambassador London 26'
Raymond is the Co-Founder of Majulah Abroad & VC Partnerships & Program Manager at Qapita. In his undergrad, he participated in 3x Overseas Internships and 1x Exchange across 4 cities (Singapore, Shanghai, Silicon Valley, London) and 3 continents, where he worked across Software Engineering, Growth and Partnership roles.
